title: Set-system sparsifiers of size proportional to chain length
formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(C>0\) such that for every integer \(m\ge 1\), every family \(S\subseteq 2^{[m]}\), every weight vector \(w\in \mathbb{R} \ge 0^{m}\) and every \(0<\varepsilon <1\), there is a reweighting \(\tilde\{w\}\in \mathbb{R} \ge 0^{m}\) with at most \(C\cdot CL(S)/\varepsilon ^{2}\) nonzero coordinates and satisfying \((1- \varepsilon )\sum _{i\in A}w_{i}\le \sum _{i\in A}\tilde\{w\}_{i}\le (1+\varepsilon )\sum _{i\in A}w_{i}\) simultaneously for every \(A\in S\)?
why: Would give a sharp structural bound for simultaneous multiplicative compression of arbitrary weighted set families. It asks whether chain length and squared inverse accuracy fully account for the necessary support, without logarithmic losses.
status_note: Published definitions, main bound and Conjecture 23 checked through 11 September 2026, together with the related May 2026 report and subsequent searches. No matching logarithm-free universal bound or counterexample was located.

progress.text: The ICALP paper proves a universe-size-independent bound with logarithmic overhead and poses the \(O(CL(S)/\varepsilon ^{2})\) bound as Conjecture 23.
A related CSP sparsification report still states its broad characterizations with polylogarithmic and accuracy factors; its abstract does not settle the sharper conjecture.

importance.reason: A general multiplicative sparsification conjecture linking support size to a structural invariant, with consequences for cuts, codes and CSPs. The existing numerical score is retained during formulation review.

sentences: A sparsifier retains and reweights a few coordinates while approximately preserving every set’s total weight.
The conjecture asks for a support bound proportional to chain length divided by \(\varepsilon ^{2}\).
Chain length is measured through the union-closure, so even an incomparable collection of singleton sets can have large chain length.
The published upper bound has extra logarithmic factors, which are precisely the remaining loss in the question.
A resolution would establish whether this structural parameter completely controls multiplicative sparsification up to a universal constant.

references.title: Multiplicative Error Set System Sparsification: A Simpler Proof via Chain Length Contraction
references.authors: Brakensiek, Joshua; Guruswami, Venkatesan; Putterman, Aaron

definitions: Here \([m]=\{1,\ldots ,m\}\), and S is any finite collection of subsets, including possibly the empty collection. The support of w̃ is \(\{i:\tilde\{w\}_{i}>0\}\); coordinates outside it are dropped, while retained coordinates may receive arbitrary nonnegative real weights. No normalization such as \(\sum w_{i}=1\) is imposed. Following the source’s witness definition, a chain of length \(\ell\) consists of distinct coordinates \(a_{1},\ldots ,a_{\ell}\) and distinct sets \(A_{1},\ldots ,A_{\ell}\in S\) with \(a_{i}\in A_{i}\) for every i and \(a_{j}\notin A_{i}\) whenever \(i<j\). \(CL(S)\) is the maximum possible \(\ell\), allowing \(\ell =0\). Equivalently, take the union-closure \(U(S)=\{\bigcup T:T\subseteq S\}\), including the empty union; \(CL(S)\) is the largest number of strict inclusions in an ascending chain starting from \(\varnothing\) in \(U(S)\). Thus \(CL(S)=0\) when S is empty or contains only \(\varnothing\). It is not merely the largest chain in the original family. A \((1\pm \varepsilon )\) sparsifier is a reweighting satisfying the simultaneous inequalities in the statement. Sets of original weight zero must retain weight exactly zero. All data and weights are quantified mathematically; the question places no running-time, oracle-access, randomness or bit-complexity requirement on finding w̃. The same C must work independently of m, S, w and \(\varepsilon\). The source allows \(\varepsilon >0\); values \(\varepsilon \ge 1\) admit the zero reweighting, so restricting the nontrivial question to \(0<\varepsilon <1\) preserves it.
answer_criterion: Prove the universal existence bound with one absolute constant C, or refute it by showing that for every C there are a family, weights and an accuracy parameter for which every multiplicative sparsifier needs more than \(C\cdot CL(S)/\varepsilon ^{2}\) coordinates. Bounds with an additional unbounded logarithmic factor do not meet the conjecture; an efficient construction is not required.

context_blocks.title: Preserve all set weights with fewer coordinates
context_blocks.text: A coordinate can represent an edge, a constraint or a position of a codeword. A sparsifier removes coordinates and compensates by reweighting those it keeps. The same reweighting must preserve every specified set’s weight, including small-weight sets, which makes multiplicative error stronger than a global additive-error allowance.

context_blocks.title: One set can be represented by one weighted coordinate
context_blocks.text: If S contains only the whole nonempty universe, its chain length is one. Placing the entire total weight on any one coordinate preserves that sole set weight exactly. A large universe alone therefore does not force a large sparsifier.

context_blocks.title: Union-closure sees constraints absent from direct containment
context_blocks.text: If S consists of all m singleton sets, the original sets are pairwise incomparable. Their unions nevertheless form a chain of m strict inclusions, so \(CL(S)=m\). With unit original weights and \(\varepsilon <1\), every singleton must retain positive weight; all m coordinates are necessary. This explains why the conjecture uses chain length in the union-closure.

context_blocks.title: The current upper bound still has logarithmic overhead
context_blocks.text: The paper gives support \(O(CL(S)\cdot \log ^{2}(CL(S)/\varepsilon )\cdot (\log  \log (CL(S)/\varepsilon ))^{2}/\varepsilon ^{2})\), with the usual constant-size adjustments to logarithms near one. This already removes dependence on the universe size from the overhead. Conjecture 23 asks whether all remaining logarithmic factors can be removed.

context_blocks.title: Existence and computation remain separate
context_blocks.text: The source notes that its main existence bound is not efficiently implementable in full generality. The conjecture itself only asks whether a small reweighting exists. Proving such a bound for every set family would already sharpen broad cut, code and constraint sparsification principles.
